**Given Data:**
- Resistance ($R$) = $10\ \Omega$
- Inductance ($L$) = $13\text{ mH} = 13 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H}$
- Capacitance ($C$) = $150\ \mu\text{F} = 150 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}$
- Voltage ($V$) = $100\text{ V}$
- Frequency ($f$) = $50\text{ Hz}$

**1. Inductive Reactance ($X_L$):**
$$X_L = 2 \pi f L = 2 \times \pi \times 50 \times 13 \times 10^{-3} = 4.084\ \Omega$$

**2. Capacitive Reactance ($X_C$):**
$$X_C = \frac{1}{2 \pi f C} = \frac{1}{2 \times \pi \times 50 \times 150 \times 10^{-6}} = 21.22\ \Omega$$

**3. Impedance ($Z$):**
Net reactance $X = X_L - X_C = 4.084 - 21.22 = -17.136\ \Omega$ (Capacitive)
$$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + (-17.136)^2} = \sqrt{100 + 293.64} = 19.84\ \Omega$$
In polar form: $Z = 10 - j17.14\ \Omega = 19.84 \angle -59.7^{\circ}\ \Omega$

**4. Current ($I$):**
$$I = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{100}{19.84} = 5.04\text{ A}$|

**5. Power Factor ($\cos \phi$):**
$$\cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{10}{19.84} = 0.504 \text{ (leading)}$$

**6. Power Consumed ($P$):**
$$P = V I \cos \phi = 100 \times 5.04 \times 0.504 = 254.01\text{ W}$|
*(Alternatively: $P = I^2 R = (5.04)^2 \times 10 = 254.01\text{ W}$)*
proTip: Pay close attention to whether the net reactance is inductive or capacitive so the power factor phase angle nature (lagging/leading) is correctly stated.
